verdict.rationale: Zep's pricing page advertises deployment in 'Your VPC', which suggests running on infrastructure you control. Separately, Zep ships Graphiti, its open-source temporal knowledge graph framework that runs locally, and the community acknowledges it as open source. However, nothing shows the full Zep memory layer (users, threads, Context Blocks) can be self-hosted from open-source code, and there are no Docker or self-hosting instructions. missing for 10: open-source self-hostable Zep server (not just the Graphiti library), Docker or deployment documentation, VPC deployment details, independent hands-on self-host corroboration

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the memory layer from open-source code (e.g. via Docker) on infrastructure I control

citations.quote: Graphiti is the open-source temporal knowledge graph framework. Use it to build and query a single Context Graph per subject locally
Thank you for open sourcing this!
